structured_output.world_model: The results table has one row: the template baseline (64 images, 3 steps) scores 0.012 accuracy in 0.14 s. It tells me nothing about the real recipe's speed or accuracy, so every forecast below extrapolates from priors, not from measured differences. From the task text, the only reference number is a 59.3 s ResNet9 at 40 epochs. An airbench96-style net at 9 epochs on an A100 should take roughly 8-12 s eager. The main risk is that CIFAR-100 accuracy lands near 0.74-0.76, so a first port may miss 0.753. I treat the claimed 9 epochs and 0.753 as optimistic.

forecasts.reason: The port is plausible, but the reference accuracy was never measured here. It is about a coin flip whether it clears 0.753 at 9 epochs, and eager timing is uncertain.
A half epoch changes time by about 5-6% and accuracy by about 0.3 pp. That is about the size of the seed noise, so the slope is hard to pin down.
Compiling plus a fused optimizer likely saves 10-20% per step, but compile mismatches or recompiles could eat the gain.
The expected gain is about 0.2 pp, which is within the noise. The extra time is small.
Time noise is probably under 2%. Per-seed std is likely 0.2-0.4 pp.
Dropping the ragged batch and warming every shape avoids recompiles, so it probably saves 0.2-0.5 s.
Muon is untuned here and adds Newton-Schulz overhead. The 10% epoch saving is unlikely to show up in a first try.
Progressive resizing probably saves 10-15% of time and costs about 0.3-0.5 pp of accuracy. Lower-resolution shapes may add recompile overhead.
